title: Align overload protection with cost-efficient batching tier (avoid timeout/error regressions)
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Problem
- The cost-efficient batching tier intentionally increases batching aggressiveness (larger effective batches / longer queue delay). During load spikes or when concurrency is higher than provisioned throughput, we observed a failure mode where request queue delay grows until client-side timeouts, driving up 499/504-like behavior and elevated retries.
- Our existing overload protection (admission control + circuit breaker) is tuned for “standard” behavior and does not sufficiently account for tier-specific queue delay budgets and KV-cache pressure behavior.

Goal
- Ensure cost-efficient tier interacts correctly with overload protection (load shedding/circuit breakers) and does not increase error rates relative to standard at similar throughput/utilization.

Scope
- Tier-aware thresholds for overload protection signals: queue delay, in-flight request caps, KV cache pressure, and per-route timeouts.
- Explicit shed reason codes + metrics/labels to debug tier-related shedding.
- Guardrails for streaming routes (avoid shedding mid-stream unless connection is already failing; prefer pre-admission rejection).
- Canary validation criteria + rollback thresholds for staged enablement.

Non-goals
- Designing a new scheduling algorithm. This is alignment/hardening of existing overload components with tiered defaults.

Background / context
- Cost-efficient tier is expected to trade p95 latency for lower $/token. It is not expected to trade correctness/reliability (timeouts/5xx).
- Customer reports and internal beta notes mention higher timeouts when trying cost-efficient tier, especially when concurrency is near the top of provisioned capacity.

Links
- Confluence PRD: workload-aware-batching-defaults-prd
- Confluence design spec: workload-aware-batching-defaults-design-spec
- SRE SLO tiers: latency-slo-tiers-fast-standard-costefficient
- Related runtime PRs: redwood/pr_18435 (tier mapping), redwood/pr_18449 (metrics), redwood/pr_18488 (this work)

Acceptance criteria
1) Reliability parity guardrail
- For canary workloads and perf suite, cost-efficient tier must not exceed standard tier by more than:
  - +0.10% absolute on (5xx + upstream timeout) rate, and
  - +0.20% absolute on client-cancel/timeouts attributable to server queueing (see metric definitions below)
  measured over 60 minutes at comparable offered load.

2) Tier-aware overload behavior
- Overload protection must apply earlier for cost-efficient once queue delay crosses a tier-defined budget (reject early rather than allow queue delay to accumulate to timeout).
- Admission control should incorporate KV cache pressure limits to avoid OOM/evictions spirals under high concurrency.

3) Observability
- Add/verify metrics:
  - overload_shed_total{tier,reason,route,model,region}
  - overload_admit_total{tier,route,model,region}
  - overload_circuit_open{tier,route,model,region}
  - queue_delay_ms histogram already added in ENG-18422; ensure it is tagged with tier + route.
- Add trace annotations for shed reason and tier in request spans.

4) Safe rollout
- Feature-flagged and compatible with explicit batching overrides (explicit config still wins; overload protection still applies).
- Document rollback signals for SRE/on-call (what dashboards to watch; thresholds; who owns pause/rollback).

Implementation notes (proposed)
- Define tier queue-delay budgets used by overload controller (distinct from scheduler max_queue_delay_ms):
  - fast: budget ~ 5–10ms (reject early under overload)
  - standard: budget ~ 20–35ms
  - cost-efficient: budget ~ 35–60ms but with a hard cap tied to request timeout headroom (avoid letting queue consume most of deadline)
- Circuit breaker logic:
  - Open when (p95 queue_delay_ms over 1–5m window) exceeds tier budget OR (shed rate exceeds threshold) OR KV cache pressure > threshold.
  - When open, prefer HTTP 429 (rate limited) or 503 (overloaded) depending on route policy; include Retry-After for hosted where applicable.
- KV cache pressure coupling:
  - Add per-tier soft/hard thresholds that trigger gradual shedding before memory pressure causes latency explosion.

Test plan
- Unit tests for tier-to-overload-threshold mapping (including explicit override precedence).
- Load test in staging:
  - chat streaming: validate no mid-stream shedding; increased pre-admission rejects during overload.
  - non-streaming chat/completions: validate early reject prevents queue-based timeouts.
  - embeddings route: ensure batching changes don’t cause bursty overload oscillations.
- Perf-canary hook: run a fixed “overload ramp” scenario and assert error-rate deltas remain within acceptance criteria.

Rollout
- Enable tier-aware overload protection for cost-efficient tier only (initially), behind flag.
- Staged ramp by model+region:
  - 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 30–60 min holds; pause on thresholds.

Owner(s)
- Runtime: Omar El-Sayed (implementation)
- SRE partner: Rafael Mendes (rollout + alerts)
- Scheduling: Sofia Ivanova (review mapping/thresholds)
- Telemetry: Logan Wright (metric tagging sanity)

Open questions
- For hosted: should we bias toward 429 vs 503 for cost-efficient sheds to avoid retry storms?
- Should the cost-efficient tier have a stricter per-request deadline budget (server-side) to protect overall system health?
comments: 2025-02-12 — Rafael Mendes: Marking as P0. We had a brief spike during beta ramp where queue delay climbed and then we saw timeouts before circuit breaker tripped. Need earlier reject for cost-efficient so we fail fast (429/503) instead of letting requests sit in queue until client cancels.

2025-02-13 — Sofia Ivanova: Agree. Important distinction: scheduler max_queue_delay_ms is a *formation* knob; overload protection needs its own budget that accounts for route timeouts and streaming cadence. For streaming, do not shed mid-stream; do admission decision before first token.

2025-02-14 — Omar El-Sayed: Drafted approach: add tier-aware “queue_delay_budget_ms” and “kv_pressure_soft/hard” into overload_guard config. For cost-efficient, budget is higher than standard but bounded by (request_deadline_ms - decode_min_headroom_ms). Will include reason codes: QUEUE_BUDGET, KV_PRESSURE, CIRCUIT_OPEN, INFLIGHT_CAP.

2025-02-18 — Logan Wright: Please ensure metrics include tier label and route. We’ve had cases where a missing label made dashboards unusable. Also suggest adding a counter for admits so we can compute shed rate without relying on request totals.

2025-02-20 — Rafael Mendes: For shed semantics: prefer 429 on hosted (clients treat as backpressure), but 503 is acceptable for private deployments where customer ingress expects it. Add a config flag per deployment mode if easy; otherwise default 429 for hosted only.

2025-02-24 — Omar El-Sayed: Implemented in redwood/pr_18488. Added overload_shed_total + overload_admit_total + overload_circuit_open with labels (tier, reason, route, model, region). Also tags queue_delay histogram with tier/route when present in request context. Added trace annotation overload.shed_reason and overload.tier.

2025-02-26 — Sofia Ivanova (review): Looks good. Minor: the queue budget for cost-efficient should not exceed 60ms for streaming prefill path; otherwise first-token p95 suffers. Please clamp for streaming routes. Also, ensure explicit batching overrides don’t disable overload budgets.

2025-02-27 — Omar El-Sayed: Addressed clamp for streaming routes (streaming_queue_budget_cap_ms=25). Explicit batching overrides still apply to scheduler formation knobs only; overload remains active and tier is derived from effective config if tier is set, otherwise default to standard.
2025-03-03 — Leila Farouk: Added staging load test scenario and CI smoke to validate no mid-stream shedding (assert no shed_reason emitted after first_token_sent=true).

2025-03-05 — Rafael Mendes: Ran staged ramp in us-east for 2 models. Observed: cost-efficient shed rate rises earlier under overload but timeout/cancel rate drops vs previous build. No 5xx increase. Green to proceed to full ramp with standard rollback thresholds.
2025-03-07 — Connor O'Brien: Included in runtime-1.21 train. Release notes should call out new shed reason codes/metrics for debugging tier behavior.
